You are comparing two drafts written from the same brief. Read no other file, and do not run commands or browse; judge only the text below.

Brief: Write the README's opening paragraph and its Install and update section for the `tidy-hooks` plugin.

<<<DRAFT A
`tidy-hooks` is a Claude and Codex plugin that blocks `git commit` when staged files contain merge markers. If Node.js is missing, the hook lets commits proceed.

## Install and update

### Claude

Add the marketplace, then install the plugin:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add example/tidy
claude plugin install tidy-hooks@tidy
```

To update:

```sh
claude plugin update tidy-hooks@tidy
```

### Codex

Add the marketplace, then install the plugin:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add example/tidy
codex plugin add tidy-hooks@tidy
```

Review and trust the plugin hooks. Codex skips them until you do.

To update:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade tidy
```

Then restart Codex.
DRAFT A>>>

items.title: Thinking
items.text:
I'm comparing the two answers, and the main difference is where each puts the Node.js caveat. Response A mentions it in the opening paragraph, while B tucks it at the end of the Codex section, which makes it look Codex-only even though it applies to both hosts. On the update steps, B's wording of running the command and then restarting Codex reads more clearly than A's ordering. Overall I think A is the better answer.

I'm weighing whether the Node.js caveat being in A's opening paragraph should tip the reader toward A, since B's placement under Codex could make Claude users miss it. The reader can install either way, so I'm not fully sure it's a real difference, but I'll go with A.
